about: Competitive land mines: vendor-neutral success criteria where the Zscaler platform stands apart, proved by tests. 'why' and 'ask' are customer-facing and never name a vendor. 'se' notes are for the SE only, drafted from public positioning and NOT verified: confirm with competitive intelligence before relying on them.
se_status: Draft, not verified: check with competitive intelligence.

differentiators.title: Inspects all of it, not just web traffic
differentiators.why: Threats and data move on any port and through encrypted DNS. Inspecting only web traffic leaves a gap an attacker or a careless app can use.
differentiators.ask: Show TLS inspection of traffic on a non-standard port, and control of DNS over HTTPS, from the endpoint agent, with no extra appliance.

se.prisma: Probe: which traffic the agent steers and decrypts by default, and whether non-web ports are inspected inline or only firewalled.
se.netskope: Probe: whether non-web traffic needs a separate steering mode or product (cloud firewall) to be inspected, and how DoH is handled.
se.cisco: Probe: whether DNS-layer protection and full proxy inspection are separate components, and what covers DoH from the agent.
se.cloudflare: Probe: what the agent sends through the gateway by default, and whether TLS on non-standard ports is decrypted and inspected.

differentiators.title: One agent, the same policy, on any network
differentiators.why: Users work from home, hotels and offices. Protection that changes with the network, or needs a VPN, is protection that fails when people travel.
differentiators.ask: Run the same tests from the office and from home Wi-Fi with no VPN: show identical results, internet and private apps, from one agent.

se.prisma: Probe: how many agents or modes cover internet, private apps and experience monitoring, and whether policy differs on and off network.
se.netskope: Probe: whether private access and internet security use one agent and one policy, and how experience monitoring is licensed.
se.cisco: Probe: how many clients or modules are installed for secure internet, private access and experience monitoring.
se.cloudflare: Probe: digital experience monitoring depth (hop-by-hop path) compared with ZDX.

differentiators.title: Private apps stay invisible
differentiators.why: An app that can be reached can be attacked. Connecting users to one app, not the network, removes the attack surface and stops lateral movement.
differentiators.ask: Show a user reaching one private app and nothing else on that server or network, with no inbound port open to the internet.

se.prisma: Probe: whether private access is per-app or network-level for the tested setup, and what is exposed inbound.
se.netskope: Probe: whether access is scoped to app and port, and what a user can reach on the same server.
se.cisco: Probe: whether access is per-app or a network tunnel in the tested mode, and what lateral movement is possible.
se.cloudflare: Probe: how app scoping is set up (tunnel routes versus per-app), and what else a user can reach on that network.

differentiators.title: Unknown files are held until they're proven safe
differentiators.why: Allowing a never-seen file while it's analyzed means patient zero gets it. Holding it until the sandbox verdict stops it first time.
differentiators.ask: Download a file no one has seen before and show it held until the sandbox verdict, not delivered and checked later.

se.prisma: Probe: default behavior for first-seen files during analysis in the tested setup (hold versus allow and alert).
se.netskope: Probe: whether first-seen files are held inline or allowed while sandboxed, and at what file sizes.
se.cisco: Probe: whether the sandbox verdict blocks the first download or only later ones.
se.cloudflare: Probe: whether sandboxing holds the first download, and which file types it covers.

differentiators.title: AI security proven on their own AI, live
differentiators.why: AI risk is specific: prompt injection on their own apps, sensitive data in prompts, and AI tools nobody approved. It should be shown working, not described.
differentiators.ask: Attack your own AI application with prompt injection and data-leak prompts, and show each one blocked; show sensitive data stopped in a GenAI prompt and an unapproved AI tool isolated.

se.prisma: Probe: whether runtime protection for the customer's own AI apps is part of the same platform and policy, or a separate product.
se.netskope: Probe: whether protection covers the customer's own AI app (prompt injection), not only use of public GenAI.
se.cisco: Probe: how AI app protection is delivered and whether it can be shown on the customer's own app in the POV.
se.cloudflare: Probe: whether AI protection covers prompt injection on the customer's own app and data in GenAI prompts with the same policy.
